appraisal_events.evidence: "j'avais eu de la facilité, jeune, et Bergotte avait trouvé mes pages de collégien « parfaites », mais au lieu de travailler, j'avais vécu dans la paresse... j'entreprenais mon ouvrage à la veille de mourir, sans rien savoir de mon métier"; "Là où je cherchais les grandes lois, on m'appelait fouilleur de détails."
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's retrospective account diminishes his own standing as a writer: an early promise marked by Bergotte's praise was squandered through years of idleness, his mature project is begun too late and without mastery of craft, and his readers misread his search for broad laws as mere detail-hunting.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator presents himself as a belated, self-blaming figure who wasted early promise and now begins his life's work at the edge of death, without technical mastery.
His readers misunderstand the nature of his undertaking, mistaking his search for grand, distant truths for narrow fact-grubbing, which weakens how his intellectual project is perceived.

ambiguities: This passage is almost entirely interior and philosophical rather than interpersonal; the sole tracked movement is self-narrated diminishment by the narrator about himself, with Bergotte's youthful praise functioning only as contrastive background rather than a distinct evaluative act by another character. Most of the passage (illness, memory loss, meditations on mortality and the nature of the future work) contains no evaluative/social status movement between named characters and was left unannotated accordingly.
